latest.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 11
latest.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 11

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This is a test build for one pilot tester (JJ), not a public release: the GitHub prerelease
is how you install it and how the new-build banner inside Narrator gets tested.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b11-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b11.exe` and run it. Installing over a running Narrator
now works: the installer closes the app for you before replacing its files. You do not
need to quit Narrator first, but please confirm this for us and say whether the
installer asked you anything along the way. Projects, voice profiles, settings and
downloaded models under `%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Jobs can no longer run away.** Every take has a per-line token cap; a take that hits
  the cap is marked runaway and rejected instead of being kept. A cloud job that runs
  more than 3 minutes past its quoted time is cancelled by Narrator on its own.
- **A script check before you spend anything.** It warns about sentences over 25 words
  (and shows where they would split) and about lines whose subject overlaps your voice's
  reference clip, which is a known trigger for a run-on take. It only warns; nothing is
  blocked. Agents get a `check_script` tool to run the same check.
- **Quieter room tone by default, and a new de-esser dial.** New projects start with room
  tone at 0.10 and the de-esser at 0.2, both chosen by ear; overall loudness is unchanged.
  Existing projects keep the sound they already had. Both dials are on the soundscape page.
- **A chime when a job finishes**, plus a desktop notification if Narrator's window is in
  the background.
- **Sound levels on the soundscape are now measured, not guessed.** Every sound sits at a
  level in LU relative to your narration (background bed -18, an effect -8, a spoken line
  0), with a button to normalize a whole scene and a way for an agent to set one item's
  level.
- **Agents can make Narrator play what they just changed**, and can read what you last
  clicked or selected, so "play this one" and "what is this" both work without you having
  to describe the clip.
- **Audio inspection now covers sections, the timeline and sound assets**, with loudness
  and a map of where the silence is, and a transcribe tool lets an agent hear what a
  recording actually says using Narrator's own recognizer instead of an outside service.
- **A short tutorial** plays once per version from a welcome screen and from Help.
- **Installing over a running Narrator on Windows now works** (see the Windows section
  above).

## What to try

- Install this build over your running beta 10 on Windows. Tell us whether it asked you
  anything, or just worked.
- Check whether the new-build banner appeared while beta 10 was running. If it did not,
  open About, press **Check now**, and send us the exact error text it shows.
- Before your next data deck, re-record your voice reference on a subject you will not be
  narrating.
- Play with the room tone and de-esser dials on the soundscape page and tell us what you
  hear.

## Known limits

- Voices made before Beta 6 still carry the stray sound at the start of
  sentences: delete the voice and create it again from the same recording,
  which is kept under Voices.
- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 10
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 10

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update comes from two days of using Beta 9 with testers: repairs are now whole-line takes
you can swap in, the Export page tells you when the files need making again, comparing two
stretches of a recording is a real side-by-side, the Soundscape page shows the video it is
scoring, and two guides explain how to record and how to review.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b10-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b10.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Repairs are whole-line takes.** The review list shows one row per line. A repaired
  line's takes panel gains "Round 2 (repair)" with Take 1 to N cards, each the whole line
  stitched, and Use swaps the line to it. A line with a newer take reads "new take
  available, press t" until you open its panel, which outlines the new cards once.
- **Playback stops on the line.** A line no longer spills into the first words of the next.
- **Previews keep everything.** Every onboarding preview is kept; the player holds the gate's
  pick and a Take 1 / Take 2 button plays that whole reading in the same player. Switching
  screens pauses playback. "Record this line" now says what it does.
- **Phone recordings import.** M4A, AAC and CAF from an iPhone, 3GP, AMR and OPUS from
  Android, are decoded on upload. The custom reading passage has a limit and a word count.
- **The agent greets with a banner and a menu.** Paste "Say hello to Narrator and tell me what
  we can do" and a connected agent answers with a small banner, two things that are actually
  pending, an open door, and a question. No lists of names.
- **Recording guide.** A button in the rail on the Voices page and the voice studio, and in
  the welcome box on Home: how to record it clean, what a good clip sounds like, hearing it
  in your voice, working with an agent. Saving an alternate persona drafts its transcript.
- **Review guide.** A button on the Review page opens four short sections: listen, mark it
  (good, off and bad are markers for you; use another take and mark it good again before
  generating anything), notes, and finishing. Its keys never reach the project behind it.
- **Files that need making again say so.** The Export page shows a banner and outlines
  "Create MP4 and audio files" when a take, section, soundscape, timeline or finishing
  setting changed since the files were created, from what the delivery recorded rather than
  from timestamps. Files from an earlier version read as unknown until made again. The
  Soundscape page shows the same warning and points to Export.
- **Comparing two stretches of a recording.** Audio inspection compares excerpts within one
  recording side by side: a visible selection on the waveform with exact range inputs,
  A and B audition buttons next to each other, one audio at a time, and only the changed
  side updates. Transcript drafts, provenance and exports are unchanged.
- **Soundscape shows its video.** A muted preview of the project's MP4 sits above the
  timeline and follows the master voice track's play, pause, seek and reset. Clip timing,
  gain and fades are easier to reach; the layout holds at desktop and phone widths.
- **Preview and repair fixes.** History previews cannot be swapped while a preview is
  generating, including after a cloud quote is confirmed, and a pill chosen by keyboard
  keeps focus after its clip loads. Using a whole-line take is one change with one undo,
  and a parked repair is never adopted by a refused Use. Keys in the takes panel act on the
  card you last clicked. A phone recording whose conversion times out is refused cleanly.
- **Settings.** The agent step restarts, reconnects and verifies in place. A project's spend
  cap can be cleared. Home's next step reads "Generate" for a project with no audio yet.
- **Agent fixes.** A plain sentence when Narrator is not running; start_here first in the tool
  list and naming the project it means; a summary from source_overview instead of raw bins;
  the within-the-cap line counts the shared pool; a first-run-on-the-GPU line.

## Known limits

- Voices made before Beta 6 still carry the stray sound at the start of
  sentences: delete the voice and create it again from the same recording,
  which is kept under Voices.
- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 9
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 9

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update is for people who drive Narrator from an AI agent (Claude Code,
Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex and others over MCP). The agent can now run cloud
work on its own inside a spend cap you set, it knows where to start, and the
guide it reads leads with the repair loop.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b9-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b9.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **The spend cap replaces the click.** An agent's cloud quote runs on your word
  in chat while the project stays under its cap, counting everything already
  spent or reserved. Over the cap, the quote waits in the approvals card as
  before. A project with no cap of its own draws from the default in Settings
  (2.00 USD), which is one shared pool across every such project, so an agent
  cannot start new projects to get a fresh budget. Leave the default empty to
  confirm every cloud job by hand.
- **Read this if you set a cap before Beta 9.** A cap used to only block runs
  above it. It is now also permission: agents may spend up to it without
  asking. If you set a project cap as a hard stop, lower it or clear the
  default in Settings.
- **The cap is where you can see it.** It sits on the project's generation
  card, showing the default when the project has none. Only a person can
  change it; the agent's tools refuse to.
- **Approve and raise in one click.** When a quote would pass the cap, the
  approvals card offers "Confirm and raise the cap to $X", and says that agents
  may then spend up to $X on that project without asking.
- **Agents know where to start.** A `start_here` tool returns your voices,
  your projects with what is pending on each (verdicts, stale chunks, running
  jobs, quotes awaiting approval, spend against cap), and one suggested next
  step. The Agents card's verification prompt asks for it.
- **Prompts read as goals.** "I want to narrate a document", "I want to fix the
  chunks I marked", and six more, including a "get started" prompt.
- **Milestones.** The first generation, the first MP4 and a rebuild at 0 ms
  drift each come back with one line the agent relays.
- **The guide leads with the loop.** The workflow guide every agent loads now
  opens with Start here, the repair loop (listen, flag, repair one chunk,
  splice, rebuild, re-listen), the money rules and how to report numbers; it is
  260 lines instead of 402.
- **Build fixes.** Installers build only on a release tag; a test that failed
  on slow CI runners now waits for the local job it freezes.

## Known limits

- Voices made before Beta 6 still carry the stray sound at the start of
  sentences: delete the voice and create it again from the same recording,
  which is kept under Voices.
- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 8
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 8

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update is a round of fixes from using Beta 7 end to end: clearer review
controls, skipping slides at upload, switching a project's voice without losing
work, and file creation that shows its progress like every other job.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b8-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b8.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Skip slides at upload.** The whole deck is shown as thumbnails when you set
  up a project, with a field for the slides to leave out (for example title and
  camera slides). Skipped slides carry a badge and get no narration.
- **Creating files is a tracked job.** "Create MP4 and audio files" now shows
  its stages (Stitching sections, Mastering audio, Encoding video) in the Jobs
  panel, and Review and Export follow it instead of waiting blind.
- **Review controls read as actions.** Every button says what it does and has a
  tooltip. The take you chose by ear is shown as "your pick: take N", with
  "In use" or "Gate pick, not in use" so you can see which take is in the file.
  A take plays as soon as you choose it. Repairs you parked earlier can be used
  straight from the Takes sheet.
- **Changing the label no longer re-creates the files.** Switching the label
  rewrites the MP4 in place in a few seconds.
- **Switch a project's voice without losing takes.** Each generation round
  remembers its voice; switching back restores that voice's rounds. Rounds made
  before Beta 8 are not tagged, so restore starts from the next generation.
- **Export shows what is current.** The Export screen has an MP4 player, a
  label status chip, and says whether the files are older than the latest
  takes or soundscape.
- **Soundscape.** The waveform view now handles tracks up to 20 minutes (was
  87 seconds), the muted MP4 preview follows the playhead, and "Prepare export"
  opens Export.
- **Readability and Lines screens** show a summary first with details on
  demand, and "Continue to Generate" leads on. "Where to generate" is
  preselected to the voice's default.
- **Voice on Project settings.** The project's voice is shown on its settings
  page and can be changed there.
- **"Next: ... →" in the workflow strip** points to the next step.
- **Update check** re-checks every 15 minutes and no longer serves a cached
  answer.

## Known limits

- Voices made before Beta 6 still carry the stray sound at the start of
  sentences: delete the voice and create it again from the same recording,
  which is kept under Voices.
- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 7

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update makes cloud results arrive in seconds instead of half an hour, and
carries the two Beta 6 fixes: the Mac crash on voice upload and the stray sound
at the start of every sentence.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b7-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b7.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Cloud results download in seconds.** A finished cloud job used to come down
  one file at a time, about four seconds each, so a 120-line project took over
  30 minutes to download after the GPU had finished in three. The job now ships
  its results as a single archive and the download takes about 20 seconds.
  Jobs started from Beta 6 still download the old way.
- **The job panel says Downloading while it downloads.** It used to keep saying
  In progress until the first stage of the download had finished.
- **Mac: uploading or recording a voice no longer crashes the app** (Beta 6).
- **Sentences no longer start with a stray sound** (Beta 6). Voices made before
  Beta 6 keep the old reference: delete the voice and create it again from the
  same recording, which is kept under Voices.

## Known limits

- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 6
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 6

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update fixes two faults found on 13 September: the Mac app crashed the
moment a voice was uploaded, and every generated sentence began with a stray
sound ("pss" or "th") that was not in the script.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b6-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b6.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Mac: uploading or recording a voice no longer crashes the app.** The Mac
  build was missing two files the local speech engine needs, so the first
  transcription killed the app. Every Mac build before this one had the fault,
  which also blocked generation on this computer. The Mac download is about
  180 MB larger as a result.
- **Sentences no longer start with a stray sound.** The clip Narrator keeps as
  your voice reference was cut a fraction of a second too early, while the last
  word was still sounding, and the voice engine finished that sound at the
  start of every take: a hiss after an "s", a "th" or hum after a voiced ending.
  The reference is now cut where the recording has gone quiet. Measured on the
  same passage: 14 of 14 takes started with the sound before, 0 of 14 after.
- **Voices made before this update keep the old reference.** To get the fix for
  an existing voice, delete it and create it again from the same recording or
  upload; the original recording is kept under Voices.

## Known limits

- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 5
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Beta 5

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update makes cloud generation fast enough to use. In Beta 4 a one-minute
voice preview took 25 to 37 minutes on the cloud GPU and then failed; the same
preview now finishes in about 4 minutes.

## Install or update

### Mac (Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or later)

Download `Narrator-0.1.0b5-macos-arm64.dmg`, open it and drag Narrator to
Applications. The app is unsigned and not notarized: on first launch macOS says
it cannot verify the developer. Right-click Narrator in Applications, choose
**Open**, then **Open** again. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded
models under `~/.narrator` are preserved. Intel Macs are not included in this beta.

### Windows

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b5.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Cloud jobs start with everything installed.** Each cloud job used to spend
  10 to 30 minutes installing software and downloading the speech models before
  generating a word, and the time limit then cut it off with the audio already
  made. Jobs now run on a prepared image, so that setup is gone. A voice preview
  measures about 4 minutes end to end, of which 2 minutes is waiting for a GPU
  to be assigned.
- **Cloud jobs report where their time went.** A finished cloud job records the
  same timing summary as a job run on this computer, plus how long the cloud
  took to assign a GPU and start, so slow runs can be explained rather than
  guessed at.
- **Lighter installer.** The CUDA runtime for NVIDIA graphics cards is no longer
  bundled. First-run setup offers "GPU acceleration" on machines with a suitable
  NVIDIA driver and downloads it then; other machines stay on cloud generation.
  The installer is about 300 MB instead of 2 GB.

## Known limits

- Waiting for a cloud GPU is 2 to 4 minutes on every job and is outside
  Narrator's control. Previews on this computer with an NVIDIA card are faster.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta 4
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta 4

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This update fixes cloud generation on Windows, which failed on every attempt in
Beta 3, and adds a notice inside Narrator when a newer beta is available.

## Install or update

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0b4.exe` and run it. Quit Narrator completely before
installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings and downloaded models under
`%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. If setup stops with "Unable to
execute file in the temporary directory" (Error 5), your antivirus blocked the
installer's helper: allow it in the antivirus history and run setup again. Ask
for the portable archive if that still fails.

## What changed

- **Cloud generation works.** Every cloud job sent from Windows used to stop on
  the GPU within a minute, and Narrator then reported "The system cannot find
  the path specified". Two separate faults, both fixed: the job script Windows
  uploaded had Windows line endings, which the GPU could not run, and Narrator
  mistook a job that was still waiting for a GPU for a finished one.
- **Honest job status.** The Jobs panel now says Submitted, Scheduling (waiting
  for a cloud GPU), In progress or Error, and shows the reason under a failed
  job. The review and voice preview pages say "Waiting for a cloud GPU" while
  that is the case.
- **Update notice.** When a newer beta is published, every page shows a short
  notice with a "What's new" summary and a link to the download. Installing is
  still your own action; nothing downloads by itself. "Not now" hides the notice
  for that version.
- **Version numbers.** The app reports 0.1.0b4 and the installer file name
  carries the same number, so it is clear which beta is installed.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta 3
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta 3

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This Windows update changes how the installer is delivered and makes cloud
generation set itself up from a Hugging Face token.

## Install or update

Download `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0.exe` and run it. It is about 320 MB instead of 2 GB
because GPU acceleration now downloads on first run only where it can be used, so
Windows' pre-launch scan takes seconds instead of minutes.

Quit Narrator completely before installing. Projects, voice profiles, settings
and downloaded models under `%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` are preserved.

The installer is unsigned. Windows SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your
PC"; choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

### If setup stops with "Unable to execute file in the temporary directory"

The installer unpacks a small helper into your `%TEMP%` folder and runs it.
"Error 5: Access is denied" means Windows, your antivirus, or a policy refused
to run that helper. Running as administrator does not change this. In order:

1. Check the download. `Narrator-Setup-0.1.0.exe` must match the size and
   SHA-256 in `SHA256SUMS.txt`. A partial download fails at this same step.
2. Open Windows Security, Virus & threat protection, Protection history. If the
   helper was quarantined at the time of the attempt, allow it and run setup again.
3. Use the portable download instead. Unpack `Narrator-Portable-0.1.0.7z`
   anywhere (File Explorer opens `.7z` on Windows 11 23H2 or later; older
   Windows needs [7-Zip](https://www.7-zip.org/)) and start
   `Narrator\NarratorDesktop.exe`. It runs from that folder with no installer,
   uses the same `%USERPROFILE%\.narrator` data, and can be removed by deleting
   the folder.

## GPU acceleration downloads on first run

The Windows installer no longer bundles PyTorch and its CUDA libraries, which were
4 GB of the previous download. If your PC has an NVIDIA driver that can use CUDA 12.8
(driver 525.60 or newer; 570.65 or newer recommended), the setup page downloads GPU
acceleration (2.6 GB) and then the voice model, with progress and resume. Restart
Narrator once when the page asks, and local generation is on. Without such a driver,
Narrator recognises speech on the CPU and generates audio in the cloud, exactly as
before, and the setup page explains why.

## Cloud generation setup

Settings, Generation, now only asks for a Hugging Face token. Narrator checks
the token, creates a private dataset repository named `narrator-jobs-<id>` under
your account for its job files, and shows it under the token field. The `<id>`
is derived from the token, so the same token finds the same repository again
after a reinstall, and a different token gets a fresh one.

To create the token: sign in at huggingface.co, add a payment method under
Settings, Billing (cloud jobs are pay-as-you-go), then open Settings, Access
Tokens, New token, choose the **Write** role, and paste the token into Narrator.
Read-only and most fine-grained tokens are refused with a message that says why.

## Fixes

- Windows: workspace backup no longer fails with "Source changed during archive", and
  recovery export, storage cleanup candidates and size accounting work. The Windows
  directory scan reports no file identity, which every one of these relied on.
- Windows: model setup no longer fails with WinError 448 when the user profile sits
  behind a junction (a moved or redirected user folder).
- Mac: a speech-recognition backend that fails to initialise now reports its real error
  instead of "no ASR backend installed".
- The launcher reports a port that another program already holds instead of waiting a
  minute and blaming Narrator.
- Cloud: a cancel that arrives while the request is still uploading now stops the job
  before it is billed, and a cancel that lands as the job starts is sent to the provider.
- Cloud: background job polling keeps working after cloud settings are saved, and
  starts even when the token is added after launch.
- Cloud: a persistent polling error is recorded once instead of every 30 seconds.
- Cloud billing: when a job ends, its reservation is released. Hugging Face reports no
  per-job charge, so the ledger records the elapsed-time estimate labelled "estimated"
  rather than holding the reservation forever, which eventually made the spend cap refuse
  every job while reporting nothing spent.
- Cloud: a submission you cancelled that the provider never lists is retired after the
  reconcile window, its budget released, and its quote can be confirmed again.
- Stored audio references and archive entries use forward slashes on every platform.
- Both installers, the Windows executables, the desktop window and the Mac bundle now
  carry the Narrator icon. The Windows setup wizard explains what is installed now,
  what downloads on first launch, and that a GPU is optional.

## Build

Built natively on Windows from source commit `cd5c1247dacdf1fd29d2251681c1ae43a3bb5820` (branch `feat/gpu-runtime-on-demand`, PR #2 on top of PR #1). This exact installer was installed on the build PC; the installed application passed the CPU-only acceptance, installed the GPU runtime pack through its own setup page, and generated speech on the GPU.

| Asset | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| Narrator-Setup-0.1.0.exe | 322,494,669 | 6f4bf192f6593c3a4fc4520ea126190ca08a9c380d35929ab4da31f66181472b |
| Narrator-Portable-0.1.0.7z | 316,230,972 | 42acf225df33f166c9c06a40cbe02ca65eb3a1ed1ea95ab40193777e3f0cf34c |

The installer is unsigned; when Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", choose More info, then Run anyway.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta Update
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 - Windows Beta Update

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

This Windows update fixes cloud generation and voice previews failing with `PermissionError` while preparing uploads. Narrator now excludes its local coordination lock files from the upload and keeps its submission lock held.

The Windows shutdown check now queries the launcher process without sending a console signal.

It also includes the Windows startup, desktop shutdown, recording, preview memory, and progress changes in PR #1.

## Install or update

1. Download `Narrator-0.1.0-beta.2-windows-x64.exe` from the assets below.
2. Quit Narrator completely, then run the installer using the same Windows account and existing installation folder.
3. Launch Narrator and retry the cloud preview.

There is normally no need to uninstall first. The installer preserves projects, voice profiles, settings, and downloaded models under `%USERPROFILE%\.narrator`.

The Windows x64 installer bundles its software components; model weights download separately. Cloud generation needs configured cloud settings and internet access. The installer is unsigned, as in the previous beta.

## Build

Source commit: `13abe4fd48f7368e55da30aeb2c15be0692b813b`.

Build and validation: https://github.com/Moebe1/narrator/actions/runs/34498700302

Validation passed on GitHub: 138 native Windows Python tests, 3 Edge browser tests, packaged smoke, fresh model setup, and offline CPU recognition.

The original model-cache symlink trust error (WinError 448) was not reproduced on the build runner; this release does not claim a fix for that original error.

Verify the downloaded installer using the accompanying `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

releases.name: Narrator 0.1.0 - Limited Beta
releases.notes:
# Narrator 0.1.0 — Limited Beta

Made with ❤️ by Mo

Limited Beta, do not distribute.

## Included

- Midnight and Daylight workspace, guided project workflow, contextual take review, Help and About.
- Soundscape arrangement with WAV/FLAC/MP3 imports, waveforms, layers, trimming, spaces and fades.
- Global job status and prominent workspace loading feedback.
- Friendly project names, clearer required fields, agent tools and workflow instructions.
- Workspace backup, storage inspection and recovery safeguards.
- Cloud-only operation without loading local model weights; protected launcher shutdown.

## Installation

Download the installer for your platform from the assets below. Software
components are bundled. Local model weights download separately during setup.
Cloud generation requires internet access and configured cloud settings; a
compatible local-generation GPU is not required to use cloud generation.

The Mac download targets Apple Silicon. It requires macOS 15 or later, based on the native libraries in this build. The Windows download targets x64.
Intel Mac and other architectures are not included in this beta.

These beta installers are unsigned and the Mac download is not notarized.
Operating-system trust prompts are expected. Downloads in this private repository
are available only to people granted repository access.

## Verification and limits

GitHub Actions builds each installer natively and checks that its frozen server
starts in an empty workspace without downloading models and serves its UI assets.
CI also runs Python, JavaScript and synthetic Chromium workflow tests.
Private golden-audio comparisons are run locally; their recordings are not
uploaded to GitHub. See the release review document for the exact results.

Automated checks do not certify microphone hardware, GPU inference performance,
all OS versions, or install/upgrade/uninstall behavior on end-user machines.
Minimum RAM and model-generation performance have not yet been established.

## Build verification

[All GitHub Actions jobs passed](https://github.com/Moebe1/narrator/actions/runs/34352399751) for commit `0c1a7762ae1fdbdedf8040eb8b2eb814d5e2fb03`: 1,031 Python tests, 215 JavaScript tests and 39 browser workflows passed. Four private audio tests are checked locally instead of in GitHub. Both native packaged-app smoke checks passed.

Downloads: Mac approximately 438 MB; Windows approximately 2.07 GB. Windows includes the local AI/CUDA runtime; neither installer includes model weights. Verify downloads using `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
